requirement: Offshore Wind Power Plants (OWPPs) must meet frequency and voltage operating range requirements to remain connected to the grid, as outlined in ENTSO-E RfG. These requirements are to be specified by each Transmission System Operator (TSO) but must not be less than the period for 47.5 Hz–48.5 Hz.
scope: OWPPs connected to the grid within Europe (under ENTSO-E framework)
source: ENTSO-E Requirements for Generators (ENTSO-E RfG); specific TSOs
related_domains: grid connection; electrical stability; operational requirements

requirement: achieve an accurate closed-loop regulation at the PoC to comply with grid codes.
scope: Modern Offshore Wind Power Plants (OWPPs) at the Point of Connection (PoC)
related_domains: grid integration; power system stability; control systems; regulatory compliance

requirement: frequency control based on conventional droop control and spinning reserve regulation that targets grid code compliance
scope: wind power plant level (Offshore Wind Power Plants)
related_domains: grid integration; power system stability; frequency regulation

requirement: three fundamental reactive power control modes required by grid codes
scope: total wind power plant reactive power regulation (Offshore Wind Power Plants)
related_domains: grid integration; voltage control; reactive power management

requirement: The harmonic model of the WTG should be presented in a frequency domain among various power bins, and hence the aggregation according to IEC 61400-21-1 [18] and spectral component grouping according to IEC 61000-4-7 [68] is needed.
scope: Offshore Wind Power Plant (OWPP) harmonic assessment procedure, specifically for Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) harmonic models
related_domains: power quality; grid integration; harmonic assessment; technical standards

requirement: The voltage harmonic distortion on the 66-kV bus (in some OWPP, there are 33-kV buses instead) usually has to fulfil an upper limit and, therefore, needs to be checked by harmonic study.
scope: 66-kV or 33-kV buses in Offshore Wind Power Plants (OWPP) during operation/planning phase.
related_domains: power quality; grid integration; electrical engineering

requirement: When performing an impedance-based stability analysis of a wind power plant, the study must evaluate the stability of all buses.
scope: Wind power plants (implied offshore context) during stability analysis studies.
related_domains: grid stability; power system analysis; electrical engineering

requirement: Compliance with Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) – Part 4-7: Testing and Measurement Techniques–General Guide on Harmonics and Interharmonics Measurements and Instrumentation, for Power Supply Systems and Equipment Connected Thereto.
scope: Power Supply Systems and Equipment Connected Thereto (applicable to wind farm electrical systems and grid connection)
related_domains: electrical systems; grid integration; electromagnetic compatibility; harmonics mitigation; measurement techniques
